14.​Amend paragraph 34 (London - Camden)  
 
The culture war over migration has become a Frankenstein’s monster for the establishment, 
however. Economically, restrictions on immigration are a headache for British bosses, who 
rely on a steady stream of migrant labour to hold down wages and boost profits. Previously, 
these concerns were outweighed by the super-exploitation of immigrants which a 
climate of fear helped enable, but now rhetoric of mass deportations heralds the cure 
becoming worse than the disease. As with Brexit, this issue splits the ruling class 
between a maverick layer and its sensible strategists. Politically, meanwhile, the focus 
on migration has played into the hands of right-wing populists like Farage, who the 
capitalists do not fully trust to represent their interests. And socially, it has given rise to 
far-right riots and racist attacks that only intensify the instability in British society. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject 
 
15.​Add after paragraph 34 and renumber (Cambridge UoC)  
 
Beyond the question of migration, culture wars are continuing to be stoked not only 
by the government and populist politicians but also the media and online influencers. 
For example, we have seen the rise of anti-trans rhetoric funded by billionaires like JK 
Rowling, resulting in a division in society. Whilst some have fallen prey to this 
rhetoric, others are drawing the necessary conclusions that the fight against 
oppression is one battle amongst a bigger class war. As others on the left argue 
about identity politics and shout “hope not hate”, we recognise that what underpins 
this all is capitalism and the class divide. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject 
 
16.​Amend paragraph 39 (Manchester - Withington 2) 
 
Scandals like this, in conditions like today’s, have the potential to produce social explosions. 
All it would take is a single political or labour movement leader – or some other accidental 
figure, like a celebrity – to boldly attack the establishment, and this could bring forth a mass 
movement against the government and the entire Epstein class. The fact that the left and 
trade union leaders have remained silent on this matter is a damning indictment of their 
political weaknesses. 
 
CC recommendation: Reject
